quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right side of the road ahead if oncoming drivers do not dim their lights. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You may proceed when the road is clear and it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can be dangerous to infants and small children, even in low-speed crashes.
All passengers should use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in the rear seat. Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with a front passenger airbag.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead, to the right.
Hiking trails ahead, to the right.

questions.explanation: This sign shows that hospital emergency services are located to the right.

questions.question: What can help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.

questions.explanation: Quick stops waste time and fuel because you must accelerate to match traffic speed again. Look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This improves fuel efficiency.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers to yield to trains at a railroad crossing. Do not try to drive faster than a train to cross the tracks.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On curves or hills because other vehicles are unlikely to be coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may cause a crash. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. Other drivers must be able to see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic signal means what light will appear soon?
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Re-enter the lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown (13 feet, 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with flashing signals. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when flashing signals warn of an approaching train. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of a train.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing. If a train is near or going fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, what is important to remember?

options.text: Pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.
Give yourself extra space when stopping.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your vehicle travels on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain or when water is standing on the road to keep your wheels from slipping.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. What must you do?

options.text: Drive with your flashers turned on.
Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you are approaching?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are approaching a railroad crossing.

questions.question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Allow the motorcyclist the right half of a traffic lane.
Allow the motorcyclist the entire width of a traffic lane.
Begin moving past the motorcycle before your vehicle is entirely in the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcyclist the entire width of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Give motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians plenty of space. Be extra careful when turning or changing lanes near them. A motorcyclist has the right to use the entire width of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
They do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the rear. Avoid staying in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel hard to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road gradually.
Slow down gently using the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently using the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep it off the pavement and slow down gently with the brakes. Once you are going slowly enough, turn the steering wheel to get back on the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: What helps a person recover from drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time allows a person to recover from alcohol.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: On long trips, how can you prevent drowsiness?

options.text: Move your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly. Give yourself time to rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake firmly. Pull off the road safely and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Defensive driving means:

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Getting ahead of poor drivers in traffic to stay safe.
Following the car ahead of you closely.
Changing lanes quickly to get around traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid accidents with careless, aggressive, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, shaded areas under trees or buildings freeze first and dry last. Be extra careful on these road sections.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without using its emergency lights. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you without its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Continue driving normally.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign tells drivers what they must obey. Where this sign is posted, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and on wet or slippery roads.
